clue.text: Cries from clumsy seamen on prow of boat

indicators.note: the prow is the front of a boat, so the front letter of the word boat is taken

parts.note: landlubbers, or lubbers, are clumsy, inexperienced sailors

explanation.surface: Wails go up from inept sailors at the front of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade puts the front letter before LUBBERS, though the clue mentions the seamen first.
explanation.definitionFit: To blubber is to weep noisily, so the verb in the third person matches cries.

clue.text: Wild pig in its own fat calls for old port

indicators.note: the pig is placed inside its fat, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: lard is fat rendered from a pig
a boar is a wild pig

explanation.surface: A feral hog wallowing in its own grease summons an outdated harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Larboard is the obsolete nautical term for the left side of a ship, now called port.

clue.text: Penetrate enemy defences — a significant development

definitions.meaning: a military breach of the enemy line

explanation.surface: Smashing through the opposing lines proves to be a big step forward.
explanation.definitionFit: The military sense is a forced passage through enemy lines; the figurative sense is a sudden important discovery or advance.

clue.text: Spent two notes at the carnival

parts.note: E and F are two musical notes
a fete is an outdoor festival or carnival

explanation.surface: Someone used up a couple of banknotes at the fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spent' looks like money paid out, but it means exhausted; 'notes' are musical, not banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete means worn out and feeble, an exhausted sense of spent.

clue.text: One bound on a crest of a wave, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so a soundalike is wanted

parts.note: surf is the foaming crest of breaking waves

explanation.surface: Someone leaps up riding the top of a wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One bound' suggests a leap, but it means a person tied to the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval serf was a labourer bound to work his lord's land.

clue.text: A verse that's initially puzzling

parts.note: a poem whose first letters of each line spell out a hidden word, so its initials pose a puzzle

explanation.surface: A poem that baffles the reader at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' seems to mean 'at first', but it points at the line initials that spell a message.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of poem hides a word in the opening letters of its lines, a puzzle in its initials.

clue.text: Area of land is left diminished by a foot

indicators.note: something diminished by an amount has that amount taken away, so letters are removed

parts.note: the word left in full

explanation.surface: A field shrinks after a twelve-inch strip is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diminished by a foot' removes FT from LEFT, leaving LE.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, a piece of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: Pushed into side issues

indicators.note: pushed about, these letters are jostled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shoved into side matters of lesser importance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issues' seems to be matters at hand, but it means printed versions.
explanation.definitionFit: Editions are the issues of a newspaper or book printed at one time.

clue.text: Shut up tight in the terminus

indicators.note: one word is set within the other

parts.note: a terminus is the end of a line
close can mean tight, as in a close fit

explanation.surface: Someone locked away securely at the end of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Enclosed means fenced in or confined, the sense of shut up as in imprisoned.

clue.text: Berliner's odd bits of cheese

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters (first, third, fifth, seventh) are taken from the German's description

explanation.surface: A Berlin resident's assorted scraps of cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese with a white rind.

clue.text: The time to say yes?

parts.note: the stage of life at which someone may legally agree, especially to sex or marriage

explanation.surface: A question about when agreement becomes appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the legal age at which a person may agree to sexual relations.

clue.text: Provides suitable surroundings for play

parts.note: literally arranges the stage backdrop for a drama, figuratively creates the right conditions

explanation.surface: Someone arranges the right background for a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means describes or prepares a background, literally the stage scenery for a drama.

clue.text: One is not expected to live on them

definitions.text: One is not expected to live on them

parts.words: One is not expected to live on them
parts.note: the idiom for being near collapse or death, as if standing on one's final limbs

explanation.surface: Things a person is unlikely to survive on.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on one's last legs is an idiom for being close to death or exhaustion.

clue.text: A girl superstar full of sex-appeal

indicators.note: the star word is filled with the abbreviation, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: the sun is our star, a super star
SA is an abbreviation for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A celebrity woman is brimming with allure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superstar' looks like a celebrity, but it is the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a female first name.

clue.text: A beating leaves marks on the skin

definitions.meaning: a rhythmic drumming, as in a military drum signal

explanation.surface: A thrashing leaves bruises on someone's body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beating' suggests violence, but it is a drumbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a military drum signal or rhythmic rapping and an inked design in the flesh.

clue.text: River duck with a red back

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the shape O

indicators.note: back means the word is turned backwards

parts.note: the word red taken as written

explanation.surface: A waterfowl with a crimson rear.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a river in central Europe forming part of the German-Polish border.

clue.text: Where the cat sat in the dog-house

definitions.meaning: the beginners' reading sentence about a cat sitting on a rug

explanation.surface: A cat sits inside a dog's kennel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cat sat on the mat' is a classic children's reading sentence; the phrase also means being called to account, as a soldier on a charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's primer line places the pet on a rug, and the idiom means being in trouble or up for a reprimand.

clue.text: Is he in the orchestra or dismissed?

indicators.note: the pronoun phrase sits inside the musical group

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians, like an orchestra

explanation.surface: A question whether a musician is playing or has been sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Banished means sent away or expelled.

clue.text: Double figures

parts.note: not numbers of ten or more, but the digit that means a pair, in the plural

explanation.surface: Numbers of ten or more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double figures' normally means numbers from 10 up; here it is figures that stand for 'double', the digit 2.
explanation.definitionFit: The digit 2 represents a pair, so its plural is literally figures meaning double.

clue.text: Cancel order I've put out

indicators.note: put out of shape, these letters are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone retracts an instruction they issued.
explanation.definitionFit: To override a decision is to set it aside or annul it.

clue.text: Eat out on a badly run vessel

indicators.note: out signals that these three letters are rearranged
badly signals that these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Dining out aboard a poorly managed ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges EAT to TEA and 'badly' turns RUN into URN.
explanation.definitionFit: This large metal container is used for heating water and serving a hot drink.

clue.text: Told off

parts.note: not scolded, but counted off one by one, as in telling beads

explanation.surface: Someone was scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Told off' reads as reprimanded, but 'tell' also means count, so this is counted off.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell is an old sense of count, so items told off are counted and given figures.

clue.text: The kind of power often sought by detectives

definitions.meaning: the energy that drives movement, as in an engine

explanation.surface: Investigators frequently hunt a certain form of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Motive power drives an engine, and a detective looks for the reason a suspect acted.

clue.text: Keen to find cuisine that's different

indicators.note: made different, the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eager to discover cooking that is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone keen is eager and passionate about something.

clue.text: Food course

definitions.meaning: as in hard ..., ship's biscuit or fare in general
a direction or line of action, as a sailing boat's heading

explanation.surface: A meal's dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard tack is sailors' food, and a sailing ship's heading is its course; both senses fit the four letters.

clue.text: A number given to someone to sing

definitions.text: A number given to someone to sing

parts.words: A number given to someone to sing
parts.note: a song handed to a singer, but read as the vocal part assigned to a particular voice

explanation.surface: A song handed to a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' suggests a song, but a voice part between tenor and soprano is assigned to a singer.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice, and the part written for that voice.

clue.text: Issue of time off

indicators.note: off signals the letters go wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A matter arising from a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time off' looks like leave from work, but 'off' rearranges TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue something is to send it out or give it forth.

clue.text: Mishap caused by stress — I'd go into it

indicators.note: the short phrase goes into the other word, one inside the other

parts.note: an accent is stress placed on a syllable

explanation.surface: An unfortunate event brought about by pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stress' suggests anxiety, but it is emphasis in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is an unfortunate unplanned event.

clue.text: Having receptive pupils, all agog

definitions.meaning: with eyes wide, ready to take in what is seen

explanation.surface: A class of eager students, every one of them fascinated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupils' suggests schoolchildren, but it is the eye's pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes wide apart and alert mean both attentive to sight and eagerly expectant.
